title: The Honest Woodcutter

scenes.text: A poor woodcutter's only axe falls into a deep river. He sits by the bank, worried about feeding his family.

scenes.prompt: A river spirit offers you a shining golden axe. Is it yours?

scenes.text: The woodcutter says the truth. The spirit is pleased and rewards his honesty with all three axes.
In the story, a dishonest answer loses the golden axe and the old one too. What would you do differently?

scenes.prompt: Imagine you find a magical pencil that your friend brought to school, and your friend has lost it. What would you do?

options.label: Give it back to my friend

scenes.purpose: Checks whether the child can apply the lesson to a new, real-life situation

scenes.text: Why did you choose that? How would your friend feel?

reflection_prompt: Why do you think honesty was rewarded?

pilot_observation.setting: Pilot with government-school children in Andhra Pradesh
pilot_observation.note: After the woodcutter story, children were asked the magical-pencil question and answered honestly, applying the lesson to a new situation. Small informal pilot; not a controlled study.
